literal: By fire even if burnt, escape there may be; they will not escape, great ones having offended who behave.
translation: Even if one is burnt by fire, there may be a way to survive; but those who behave offensively towards great people will never escape destruction.
modern: நெருப்பினால் சுடப்பட்டாலும் தப்பிப் பிழைக்க வழி உண்டு; ஆனால், பெரியவர்களுக்குத் தீங்கு செய்து வாழ்பவர்கள் தப்பிப் பிழைக்க மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the absolute ruin that comes from offending great people. The poet uses a powerful contrast with fire: even if a person is physically caught in a fire, there is still a rare chance of survival. However, for those who behave disrespectfully or act against great minds, there is absolutely no escape from ruin. The word 'உய்வு' refers to survival or escape, while 'பிழைத்து' here carries the meaning of committing a wrong or offense. The verse emphasizes that moral and social transgressions against the wise are far more destructive than physical elements.
